target_customer: Mobile and multiplayer game developers who want community features
problem: Mobile games bore players quickly, especially singleplayer ones; Galaxy offered a free SDK for clans, friend syncing, avatars and leaderboards.

founders.name: Adam Neuwirth
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page and launch post.

technical_complexity.rationale: Leaderboards, clans and friend sync are backend features with an SDK; engineering is standard but multi engine support adds work.

defensibility.rationale: A free SDK of common features could be copied by backend vendors and game engines in weeks.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found on incumbents copying; outcome not public.

market_need_then: YC profile reports Galaxy worked with 115 games and over 250,000 end users, which is its own claim of early use; no external demand data found.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with Galaxy Interactive, Galaxy Gameworks and others; no brand evidence found.

outcome_analysis: Galaxy was a free social SDK for games from the Winter 2021 batch with a single named founder and a two person team. The YC page marks it inactive and no news, shutdown note or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public. The brand_confusion factor is a weak inference from the generic name; no source says it mattered.
notes: No company website listed in the dataset. Seed rests on one aggregator (StartupIntros) and is probably the standard YC deal. CB Insights lists a 500K round and 2.68M total but names a different CEO, so it likely describes another Galaxy and was excluded. The Pragma competitor is a backend platform dated a few months after the batch; relevance is partial. Founded year from YC page.
